## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Phaser 4 WebGL: migrate core `GeometryMask` sites to Mask filters + scaffold `Phaser.AUTO`

Raised from `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (Main Street repo, `../tce-main-street`) on producer
instruction (2026-10-29, "separate core item in `../Tableau-Card-Engine`").

## Problem statement

Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7` made `GameObject.setMask` a **no-op under WebGL**.
`node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js:27` states
`GeometryMask` is Canvas-only; the WebGL path logs

```
Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.
```

and returns immediately, so the object renders **unclipped**.

The Main Street game repo has completed its side of the migration
(`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, commit `73cfba6c` on its `dev`) and has switched its
launcher from `Phaser.CANVAS` to `Phaser.AUTO`. That change makes this defect
live in shipped builds: the core-owned overlays below lose their scroll
clipping in any WebGL boot.

Outstanding core-owned call sites (verified 2026-10-29 against core `f0b5b9e9`):

- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — `setMask` at the scroll-region setup
  (observed at `SettingsPanel.ts:574` during a real WebGL boot)
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — `setupScrollMask` (observed at `HelpPanel.ts:386`)
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts` — `setMask` / `createGeometryMask` in the overlay dialog
  scroll region
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — `setMask`
  (reached via `GymSceneBase.initHelp`)

Additionally the scaffold generator still forces Canvas, so every downstream
game repo it generates reverts the migration:

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderMainTs()` emits `type: Phaser.CANVAS`
- the core repo's own `main.ts` likewise

## Users

- **Game players** — Help / Settings / Overlay dialogs and the Gym card index
  must stay visually correct (content clipped to its scroll region) in WebGL
  builds, not just in Canvas ones.
- **Downstream game-repo maintainers** — need the scaffold to emit
  `Phaser.AUTO` so a fresh/re-scaffolded repo does not silently regress to
  Canvas and lose access to Phaser 4's Filter/GPU-shader pipeline.
- **Maintainers** — one shared core helper instead of per-repo copies.

## Reference implementation (already proven, do not re-invent)

`../tce-main-street/src/ContainerClip.ts` is the working pattern and is the
model to port into core as a shared, exported helper:

- `createContainerClip(scene, target, rect?)` branches once on
  `scene.renderer.type`:
  - **Canvas**: unchanged `GeometryMask` (transparent fill, Graphics on the
    display list) — Canvas output stays byte-stable.
  - **WebGL**: `target.enableFilters()` then
    `target.filters.internal.addMask(graphics, false, scene.cameras.main)`,
    with an **opaque** fill and the Graphics kept **off the display list**
    (a Mask filter samples the mask texture's alpha and renders the mask
    GameObject itself).
- **`clear()` is a real "no clip"** (Canvas `clearMask`, WebGL
  `filter.active = false`). A zero-area mask is *not* a no-op — it hides the
  whole object.
- A `Container` has no intrinsic width/height, so Phaser focuses the filter on
  the camera context and the mask applies in **screen space**, matching Canvas
  `GeometryMask` semantics (fixed to the scene, not following the object).
- Tear down the clip on scene shutdown: under WebGL the mask Graphics is off
  the display list and is not disposed by the scene.
- Verified by evidence: a Mask filter **does** clip a `Container` in rc.7;
  proven with `renderer.snapshotPixel()` probes inside/outside the rect, and
  unchanged when the clipped container is translated. No per-camera-viewport
  fallback is needed.

Do not edit the Main Street repo from this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Core helper.** A renderer-aware container-clip helper exists in core
   (suggested `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts`), exported through the public `@ui`
   surface so downstream game repos can reuse it, with the `ContainerClip`
   API (`setRect`, `clear`, `destroy`) and the Canvas/WebGL branching described
   above. Its doc comment records the Phaser 4 Canvas-only `setMask`
   restriction.
2. **Sites migrated.** `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/Overlay.ts`,
   `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts`
   no longer construct a `GeometryMask` directly for clipping; all four use the
   shared helper.
3. **Scaffold emits `Phaser.AUTO`.** `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`
   `renderMainTs()` emits `type: Phaser.AUTO`, the core repo's own `main.ts`
   matches, and any scaffold test/fixture asserting `Phaser.CANVAS` is updated.
4. **WebGL browser test.** At least one browser test forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and
   asserts (a) clipping actually happens (pixel probe via
   `renderer.snapshotPixel()`) and (b) **no** `setMask … not supported in
   WebGL` warning is emitted from core code. Canvas parity is asserted in the
   same file.
5. **No Canvas regression.** Full core test suite green; Canvas rendering
   output unchanged (the Canvas branch keeps `GeometryMask`).
6. **Docs.** The renderer/mask restriction is documented (core README and/or
   `docs/`) so the next reader does not repeat the diagnosis, and the scaffold
   documentation states the emitted renderer.
7. **Downstream switch-over hand-off.** On completion, a work item is created
   (or the existing placeholder updated) in the Main Street repo
   (`../tce-main-street`) to: bump the pinned core commit in
   `configs/engine-pin.json`, run `npm run scaffold` to regenerate
   `main.ts`, re-run `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts`
   with the core-owned warnings no longer excluded, and confirm the launcher
   boots WebGL with no unclipped core overlay.
   **The follow-up already exists**: `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` ("Re-scaffold Main
   Street launcher to Phaser.AUTO and verify a clean WebGL boot once core masks
   land") in the Main Street store, currently `blocked`. Reuse/update that item
   rather than creating a second one, and leave a comment on it naming the core
   commit that satisfies this item.

## Constraints

- Do **not** edit the Main Street repo (`../tce-main-street`) from this item;
  the cross-repo hand-off is a work-item, not a code edit (AC7).
- Canvas behaviour must not change: branch on the renderer, do not replace the
  `GeometryMask` path.
- No new dependencies.
- `TestGamePool` and downstream browser tests intentionally stay on
  `Phaser.CANVAS` for CI speed (~10x faster under SwiftShader) — do not force
  them to WebGL.

## Existing state / verified facts

- Phaser pin: `4.0.0-rc.7`. `GameObject` mixes in `Components.Filters`
  (`enableFilters()`, `filters`), so any GameObject — `Container` included —
  can host a Mask filter.
- `GeometryMask` uses the Graphics **path** and ignores fill alpha; a Mask
  filter uses the rendered mask texture's **alpha**.
- `filterList.getActive()` filters on `filter.active`, so `active = false` is a
  cheap way to disable a clip without destroying it.

## Related work

- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (Main Street) — renderer migration + renderer-aware
  clips for the in-repo surfaces; delivered commit `73cfba6c`. Source of this
  item.
- `MS-0MVT4M9KM005Z0YM` (Main Street) — the original diagnosis; closed as a
  duplicate of `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`, with its core-owned part routed here.
- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` (Main Street) — the earlier core-deferral record for
  `HelpPanel` / `Overlay` / `SettingsPanel`; superseded by this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: filter cost.** Each clipped container gains a filter render step
  (context-sized for unbounded containers). Mitigation: measure in the browser
  test scene; keep the clip count small (4 sites).
- **Risk: Mask filter on a nested/transformed container.** The Main Street
  evidence covers transformed containers; re-verify per core site with a pixel
  probe rather than assuming.
- **Assumption:** headless Chromium (Playwright) provides WebGL2 in CI, so the
  WebGL browser test is viable.
data.title: Phaser 4 WebGL: migrate core GeometryMask sites to Mask filters + scaffold Phaser.AUTO
